name: veterinary_clinic_system_082_inbound_comms_triage
instruction: Triage the comms inbox and produce a route summary. Update every communications row: add field triage='needs_reply' if direction='inbound', triage='fyi' if direction='outbound'. For inbound rows, add route_to based on the subject (case-insensitive keyword match): 'lab' if the subject contains 'lab'; 'boarding' if it contains 'boarding'; 'billing' if it contains 'billing' or 'quote'; 'front_desk' if it contains 'vaccine', 'vaccines', or 'reminder'; otherwise 'general'. For outbound rows, set route_to='logged'. Then write one ops_reports row per route_to for inbound and one outbound row: {report:'comms_triage', batch_code, scope:'inbound'|'outbound', route_to, count}. The counts must be derived from the live communications after the route_to assignment.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session; placeholder for hardmode v2
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session; placeholder for hardmode v2

success_criteria.summary: All communications rows have triage and route_to set correctly. Inbound route counts are exact and match an independent SQL classification. Existing rows are byte-identical except for the two added fields. The ops_reports summary has one row per inbound route plus one outbound row for this batch.

checks.expect: triage and route_to fields set per direction and subject; all other fields unchanged
route_to counts are also derived via SQL CASE/GROUP BY and agree with the Python computation

hazards: There are 81 outbound and 79 inbound communications rows (seed_snapshot.json). A keyword-only scan that ignores direction will mis-route outbound rows such as outbound id 34 with subject 'Reminder call — vaccines due' as front_desk instead of fyi/logged.

The subject 'Discussed dental quote' (18 inbound, 11 outbound) must route to billing because of the 'quote' keyword; an agent that only looks for 'billing' in the subject will misclassify the inbound 'Discussed dental quote' rows as 'general'.
The subject 'Reminder call — vaccines due' uses 'vaccines' (not 'vaccination') and 'reminder'. A literal 'vaccination' keyword misses the 13 inbound rows and routes them to 'general'.

Inbound counts per route are: lab 10, boarding 17, billing 39 (21 'Billing question resolved' + 18 'Discussed dental quote'), front_desk 13. The ops_reports summary must be inbound-only; counting all rows by subject would double the counts with the 81 outbound rows.

The verifier compares the agent's per-route counts against a SQL GROUP BY that classifies subjects with the same keyword rules, so a hardcoded or message-derived count that does not match live data fails.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Combines a per-row classification/update task with an aggregate summary report, requiring both correct field mutation and exact per-route counts verified by SQL. Outbound rows and keyword nuances ('vaccines' vs 'vaccination', 'quote' as a billing signal) are real decoys.
